metaDescription: Six canister vacuums with motorized powerhead nozzles, from the Sebo K3's dedicated ET-1 head to Kenmore Hair Eliminator models and a budget Eureka brush.
expertTake: The Sebo AIRBELT K3 is the best powerhead canister because its ET-1 head has its own motor, a jam guard and a seven-year warranty behind it. The Kenmore 600 Series 81615 is the value pick, with a motorized Pet PowerMate and triple HEPA. Anyone with mostly hard floors should skip powerheads and choose a suction-only canister.
introParagraphs: A powerhead turns a canister into a carpet machine. Where a plain floor tool relies on airflow alone, a powerhead carries a motorized brush that spins against the pile, so it loosens embedded grit, lifts hair and leaves the pattern in the fibres. The motor sits in the head itself or is driven from the body, and that choice affects weight, cost and how the machine behaves on thick pile.

All six picks here use a motorized nozzle, and they differ in what powers it, what it does with hair and how well the machine supports it. The sections below explain those differences in plain terms, and they are written for buyers who have carpet and want a canister's reach as well.

products.name: Sebo AIRBELT K3 9687AM canister with ET-1 electric powerhead
products.description:
The K3's ET-1 is a true electric powerhead: a floor head with its own motor and a brush roller that holds its speed whatever the pile does. Power reaches it through a cable in the hose, so the body's 1250 W motor can devote itself to suction while the head handles agitation.

A built-in safety system stops the roller and signals you if something jams it, so a stray sock or a knot of hair does not burn out a belt. The head is sold for pets, and it adjusts to different pile heights, which is what a mixed carpet house needs. A 37 ft operating radius from a 25 ft cord means fewer plug changes.

The cost is weight and price, since a dedicated head and a heavy-duty body are not cheap to build. Cut hair from the roller every few weeks, change the bag at about three quarters full and keep the filters on schedule. The seven-year motor and component warranty is the strongest evidence of confidence in this group. If you live with a heavy shedder, the jam guard also protects your fingers, because you will never have to reach into a spinning roller to clear it. A dealer network for service is another quiet benefit, since a powered head is a part you may want checked every few years.
products.bestFor: Homes with a lot of carpet that want a dedicated, long-lived powerhead.
cons: Heavier and costlier than household canisters
More head to clean and service

products.name: Kenmore 600 Series 81615 canister with motorized Pet PowerMate
products.description:
The 81615 gets its agitation from a Pet PowerMate, a motorized attachment that lifts stubborn pet hair, dander and dirt, and from a second motor in the body that keeps suction strong while it runs. Two floor nozzles with the exclusive Pop-N-Go design handle bare floors, so the powered nozzle works only where you need it.

A triple HEPA filter system captures 99.97 percent of dirt, according to the listing, and a swivel head makes it steer. Compared with the Sebo it has a lighter brush motor and a shorter warranty, but it costs much less and weighs less. For medium-pile carpet it performs well.

Clear the nozzle of hair after pet weeks and keep the bag fresh. A full bag chokes the second motor and makes the powered nozzle feel weak. It is the best value powered canister in the group. Because the powered nozzle is a separate attachment, you can leave it off for bare floors and use the plain nozzle, which protects both your finish and the brush. Treat the nozzle as a wear item, and budget for a replacement brush every few years if you have long-haired pets.
products.bestFor: Medium-pile carpet and pet homes that want a powered nozzle for less.
cons: Lighter brush motor than the Sebo

products.name: Kenmore 400 Series bagged canister with Hair Eliminator nozzle, HEPA
products.description:
This 400 series machine pairs a Hair Eliminator nozzle with a sealed HEPA path. The nozzle's brush removes hair from the roller as it spins, so you spend no time with scissors, and a two-motor body keeps suction strong. The listing says the sealed HEPA path traps 99.97 percent of dust and debris down to 0.3 microns.

It is a middle step in the Kenmore range, with onboard storage that keeps the tools on the body. Compared with the 81615 it swaps the Pet PowerMate for the self-clearing brush, and compared with the Sebo it is lighter and less rugged. Carpeted homes where hair, not pile depth, is the real problem suit it best.

Still check the roller ends for stray hair and keep the filters on schedule. An early bag swap keeps the sealed path tight. The onboard storage is more useful than it sounds on a powered machine, because the nozzle, the crevice tool and the brush all have a place on the body and you stop losing them. If you vacuum stairs, the telescoping reach and the grip make a large difference.
products.bestFor: Carpeted homes where brush wrap and dander are the main problems.
cons: Lighter brush than a dedicated powerhead
Sealed path depends on a properly seated bag

products.name: Kenmore 200 Series bagged canister with Hair Eliminator nozzle, sealed HEPA

specList.label: Use
specList.value: Carpets, rugs, stairs, upholstery, hard floors

products.description:
The 200 series is the entry point to the Kenmore range, and this version includes the Hair Eliminator nozzle and a sealed HEPA path. A two-motor system delivers suction across carpets, rugs, stairs, upholstery and hard floors, and the nozzle clears its own hair.

The difference from the 400 series is mostly in the extras: fewer onboard conveniences and a plainer finish. For a first canister with a powered nozzle, it is the lowest-cost route to a sealed, HEPA, self-clearing machine in this guide. The weight and brush are the same class as its siblings.

Check the bag seating each time and clear the brush ends of stray hair. A bag near three quarters full is ready to go. A plain finish is no handicap in daily use, and the same hose, wand and nozzle designs as the dearer models mean you can buy the same bags and filters. If you outgrow it, the accessories you own may carry over to a higher series, which is worth confirming with the maker before you spend.
products.bestFor: First-time canister buyers who want a powered, self-clearing nozzle at an entry tier.
pros: Entry price within the Kenmore range
cons: Lighter brush than a dedicated powerhead

products.name: Kenmore 500 Series bagless canister with Hair Eliminator brushroll
products.description:
The 500 series is the bagless powered canister. Two motors and cyclonic technology drive a Hair Eliminator brushroll, and a HEPA filter is listed as trapping 99.97 percent of dust down to 0.3 microns, so the specification matches the bagged models.

The cyclonic cup separates heavy debris from the air, which keeps the filter cleaner, and the bagless design avoids bag costs. The cost is the emptying step, which releases dust at the bin, and a filter that needs washing. For carpet, the powered brush works as the others do.

Empty the cup over a bag held close or outdoors. Filters need washing on schedule and a full dry before refitting. A bagless powered canister loads its filter faster on carpet, because carpet is a reservoir of fine dust and the brush throws it into the airflow. If the filter looks clean but suction has dropped, check the brush and the hose for a hair plug before assuming a motor fault.
products.bestFor: Carpet owners who want a powered nozzle and no bag costs.

products.name: Eureka NEN186BL canister, 1000W, motorized brush, sealed HEPA
products.description:
The NEN186BL is the budget machine with a motorized brush, a sealed three-stage HEPA system and a retractable 17 ft cord. A 1000 W motor and swivel steering round out the specification.

The brush is smaller than the Kenmore's and does not clear itself, so hair wraps need cutting, and a bagless body means emptying and washing. It is the cheapest way to get a powered brush on a canister from a known brand in this guide, and it suits medium-pile carpet and rugs.

Weekly, free the brush of hair and wash filters on schedule, which keeps a small motor cool. It is the choice if the budget is tight and the pile is moderate. A smaller brush means more passes on thick carpet, so work slowly and overlap your strokes. Check the brush for hair before each session, because a stalled brush on a small motor heats quickly and wears the belt.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers with medium-pile carpet who want a powered brush.
pros: Motorized brush at a budget tier

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Sebo ET-1 has its own motor with a cable in the hose, so its roller holds speed whatever the pile. The Kenmore models drive a motorized nozzle from a second motor in the body. A dedicated head is stronger and costs more. Match to pile depth. A thick shag or high-pile rug stalls a light brush motor, so such carpets need the dedicated head. On medium pile and rugs, the body-driven nozzle gives nearly the same result at much less cost and weight.

The Kenmore Hair Eliminator nozzles clear hair from the roller as it spins, and the Sebo stops its roller and warns you on a jam. A plain brush wraps and stalls. For long-haired homes, self-clearing is worth real money. Look at how the hair is removed: a comb or blade that strips hair into the airflow works better than a design that only reduces wrap. Even so, an occasional check of the roller ends is wise.

A powerhead that adjusts to the pile avoids dragging on thick carpet and lifting off thin carpet. The Sebo adjusts across a wide range, while a household nozzle is tuned for medium pile. Measure your carpet before you buy. Press a ruler into the carpet and note how deep the pile is, then check the powerhead's stated range. If your house has several pile heights, an adjustable head is the better buy, since one setting rarely suits every room.

A canister with a powerhead is a menace on bare floor if the brush cannot be switched off or swapped. The Kenmore 81615 has two nozzles with Pop-N-Go, and the Sebo offers other heads. Check how you will clean your hard floors. If the head cannot be switched off, buy a second suction-only nozzle, and keep it on the body. Many owners find that having both is more useful than a single head that tries to do everything.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Weight and balance at the head
buyingCriteria.explanation: A powered head adds weight at the end of the wand. A heavy head tires the wrist on long sessions. Hold it at arm's length for a minute before you commit. A powerhead that balances well feels lighter than its weight, and a nose-heavy one feels heavier. Telescoping wands and swivel joints change the feel, so try the whole assembly, not only the head.

A powered head has bearings, brushes and a motor that wear. The Sebo's seven-year warranty and parts supply are a major advantage. Household heads have shorter cover and cheaper replacements. Ask whether the head can be sent in for service, and whether belts and brushes are sold separately. A repairable head costs less over ten years than a sealed one replaced twice.

howWeEvaluated.title: Powerhead design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared a dedicated electric powerhead with motorized nozzles driven from the body. The Sebo led. Kenmore nozzles followed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Hair management
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited self-clearing brushes and jam protection. The Kenmore Hair Eliminator models and the Sebo led.

howWeEvaluated.title: Filtration
howWeEvaluated.description: We read each listing for HEPA and sealed paths. The Kenmore 200 and 400 series and the Eureka lead on sealed systems.

howWeEvaluated.title: Service and parts
howWeEvaluated.description: We favoured brands with parts and warranty. The Sebo's seven-year cover led. Household heads were graded on cost to replace.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We read owner feedback patterns on brush wear, belt breakage and hose kinks. Relative cost only broke ties, and nothing here quotes an amount.

cards.label: Dedicated powerhead
cards.text: The Sebo ET-1 has its own motor and holds speed in thick pile. It costs more and weighs more.

cards.label: Motorized nozzle
cards.text: The Kenmore models drive the brush from the body's second motor. They cost less and suit medium pile.

howToChoose.note: Pick a dedicated head for deep carpet, and a motorized nozzle for medium pile and rugs.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a self-clearing or jam-stopping brush, a sealed system and a powered upholstery tool.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Kenmore Hair Eliminator models and the Sebo are the strongest, with the Pet PowerMate on the 81615 as a good alternative.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more on the Sebo if you have a lot of carpet and want a machine for a decade. A dedicated head and warranty pay back.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save with the Eureka or a Kenmore if the carpet is medium pile. A motorized nozzle is enough.

maintenance.why: Hair wraps the roller and stalls it. Self-clearing designs still need an occasional check.
Hair and grit collect at the bearings and burn belts and motors. Clear them.

maintenance.task: Change the bag or empty the bin
maintenance.why: A full bag chokes airflow and the second motor. A sealed path needs a seated bag.
A clogged filter cuts airflow. Dry washed filters fully.
The powered head's cable runs through the hose. A kink or crack can cut power to the head.

faq.a: A floor head with a motorized brush. It agitates carpet pile and lifts hair, which suction alone cannot do.

faq.q: Do I need a powerhead on hardwood?
faq.a: No. A spinning brush can scatter debris and scratch some finishes. Use a suction-only head or a switchable brush.

faq.q: Is the Sebo worth the price?
faq.a: For heavy carpet use, yes. A dedicated head, jam protection and a seven-year warranty reflect a machine built to last.

faq.q: Can I use a powered nozzle on stairs?
faq.a: Yes, and it helps on carpeted treads. Check the head fits the tread and the cable does not catch.

faq.q: How do I stop hair wrapping the brush?
faq.a: Choose a self-clearing design and clear the ends regularly. Long hair is the main cause.

faq.q: Do powered canisters need special bags?
faq.a: They use the maker's bags. Buy genuine bags, since poor fits break the seal and strain the motors.
